subject: Unbinding two DataTables in tabset panels behaves oddly

messages.author: c0c84142ff215f59
messages.subject: Unbinding two DataTables in tabset panels behaves oddly
parts:
Hello everyone,

I am adding a numericInput to a DataTable so I have to use javascript to bind, and unbind as these threads indicate:

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!msg/shiny-discuss/ZUMBGGl1sss/zfcG9c6MBAAJ

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/shiny-discuss/FeqU0AoTpz0

I find that if you have two DataTables in separate tabs, which both need to be bound and unbound, one won't render.

Here is an example:

library(shiny) 
library(DT) 
shinyApp( 
  ui = fluidPage(
    sidebarPanel(
      # choose dataset
      selectInput("select","Choose dataset",c("mtcars","iris"))),
    # display table
    mainPanel(
      tabsetPanel(tabPanel("one",DT::dataTableOutput('x1')),
                  tabPanel("two",DT::dataTableOutput('x2'))),
        tags$script(HTML("Shiny.addCustomMessageHandler('unbind-DT', function(id) {
          Shiny.unbindAll($('#'+id).find('table').DataTable().table().node());
        })")))), 
  
  server = function(session, input, output) { 
    # function for dynamic inputs in DT
    shinyInput <- function(FUN,id,num,...) {
      inputs <- character(num)
      for (i in seq_len(num)) {
        inputs[i] <- as.character(FUN(paste0(id,i),label=NULL,...))
      }
      inputs
    }
    # function to read DT inputs
    shinyValue <- function(id,num) {
      unlist(lapply(seq_len(num),function(i) {
        value <- input[[paste0(id,i)]]
        if (is.null(value)) NA else value
      }))
    }
    # reactive dataset
    data <- reactive({
      req(input$select)
      session$sendCustomMessage('unbind-DT', 'x1')
      get(input$select)[1:5,1:3]
    })
    data2 <- reactive({
      req(input$select)
      session$sendCustomMessage('unbind-DT', 'x2')
      get(input$select)[5:10,1:3]      
    })
    # render datatable with inputs
    output$x1 <- DT::renderDataTable({
      data.frame(data(),ENTER = shinyInput(numericInput,"numin",nrow(data()),value=NULL))
    },server=FALSE,escape=FALSE,selection='none',
    options=list(language = list(search = 'Filter:'),preDrawCallback=JS(
      'function() {
      Shiny.unbindAll(this.api().table().node());}'),
      drawCallback= JS(
        'function(settings) {
        Shiny.bindAll(this.api().table().node());}')))
    
    output$x2 <- DT::renderDataTable({
      data.frame(data2(),ENTER = shinyInput(numericInput,"numin2",nrow(data2()),value=NULL))
    },server=FALSE,escape=FALSE,selection='none',
    options=list(language = list(search = 'Filter:'),preDrawCallback=JS(
      'function() {
      Shiny.unbindAll(this.api().table().node());}'),
      drawCallback= JS(
        'function(settings) {
        Shiny.bindAll(this.api().table().node());}')))    
  }
) 

The table in the second tab won't render and a javascript error says essentially I can't unbind a table that doesn't exist. 

If I add another output that reads that input values from the second tab's DataTable's inputs everything suddenly works.

library(shiny) 
library(DT) 
shinyApp( 
  ui = fluidPage(
    sidebarPanel(
      # choose dataset
      selectInput("select","Choose dataset",c("mtcars","iris"))),
    # display table
    mainPanel(verbatimTextOutput("test"),
      tabsetPanel(tabPanel("one",DT::dataTableOutput('x1')),
                  tabPanel("two",DT::dataTableOutput('x2'))),
        tags$script(HTML("Shiny.addCustomMessageHandler('unbind-DT', function(id) {
          Shiny.unbindAll($('#'+id).find('table').DataTable().table().node());
        })")))), 
  
  server = function(session, input, output) { 
    # function for dynamic inputs in DT
    shinyInput <- function(FUN,id,num,...) {
      inputs <- character(num)
      for (i in seq_len(num)) {
        inputs[i] <- as.character(FUN(paste0(id,i),label=NULL,...))
      }
      inputs
    }
    # function to read DT inputs
    shinyValue <- function(id,num) {
      unlist(lapply(seq_len(num),function(i) {
        value <- input[[paste0(id,i)]]
        if (is.null(value)) NA else value
      }))
    }
    # reactive dataset
    data <- reactive({
      req(input$select)
      session$sendCustomMessage('unbind-DT', 'x1')
      get(input$select)[1:5,1:3]
    })
    data2 <- reactive({
      req(input$select)
      session$sendCustomMessage('unbind-DT', 'x2')
      get(input$select)[5:10,1:3]      
    })
    # render datatable with inputs
    output$x1 <- DT::renderDataTable({
      data.frame(data(),ENTER = shinyInput(numericInput,"numin",nrow(data()),value=NULL))
    },server=FALSE,escape=FALSE,selection='none',
    options=list(language = list(search = 'Filter:'),preDrawCallback=JS(
      'function() {
      Shiny.unbindAll(this.api().table().node());}'),
      drawCallback= JS(
        'function(settings) {
        Shiny.bindAll(this.api().table().node());}')))
    
    output$x2 <- DT::renderDataTable({
      data.frame(data2(),ENTER = shinyInput(numericInput,"numin2",nrow(data2()),value=NULL))
    },server=FALSE,escape=FALSE,selection='none',
    options=list(language = list(search = 'Filter:'),preDrawCallback=JS(
      'function() {
      Shiny.unbindAll(this.api().table().node());}'),
      drawCallback= JS(
        'function(settings) {
        Shiny.bindAll(this.api().table().node());}')))
    output$test <- renderPrint({
      shinyValue("numin2",nrow(data2()))
    })
  }
) 

I am guessing this is reactivity working its magic, and making sure the table exists so that the javascript function doesn't generate the error like before. Is there a more elegant way to get the first example working than adding a table that reads the inputs in the second DataTable?

Thanks

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Unbinding two DataTables in tabset panels behaves oddly
parts:
Maybe it's that the tables, like all outputs, aren't actually rendered if they're not showing. You can override this behavior in your Shiny Server function with:

outputOptions(output, "x1", suspendWhenHidden = FALSE)
outputOptions(output, "x2", suspendWhenHidden = FALSE)

outputOptions(output, "x1", suspendWhenHidden = FALSE)

Both tables render now, but when I change the selectizeInput on the sidebar, only the table in the open tab updates. 

So to reproduce:

1. Run app and see that the table in each tab has a subset of mtcars

2. Change the input on the sidebar to Iris

3. You'll notice the current table now has Iris data, but if you change the tabs the table in the other tab will still have mtcars even though Iris is selected

I'm not sure what the best way to ensure that an element in an unopened tab reacts correctly, so I would appreciate some guidance.

Kind Regards,
Carl

I find that if you have two DataTables in separate tabs, which both need to be bound and unbound, one won't render.

Here is an example:

library(shiny) 
library(DT) 
shinyApp( 
  ui = fluidPage(
    sidebarPanel(
      # choose dataset
      selectInput("select","Choose dataset",c("mtcars","iris"))),
    # display table
    mainPanel(
      tabsetPanel(tabPanel("one",DT::dataTableOutput('x1')),
                  tabPanel("two",DT::dataTableOutput('x2'))),
        tags$script(HTML("Shiny.addCustomMessageHandler('unbind-DT', function(id) {
          Shiny.unbindAll($('#'+id).find('table').DataTable().table().node());
        })")))), 
  
  server = function(session, input, output) { 
    # function for dynamic inputs in DT
    shinyInput <- function(FUN,id,num,...) {
      inputs <- character(num)
      for (i in seq_len(num)) {
        inputs[i] <- as.character(FUN(paste0(id,i),label=NULL,...))
      }
      inputs
    }
    # function to read DT inputs
    shinyValue <- function(id,num) {
      unlist(lapply(seq_len(num),function(i) {
        value <- input[[paste0(id,i)]]
        if (is.null(value)) NA else value
      }))
    }
    # reactive dataset
    data <- reactive({
      req(input$select)
      session$sendCustomMessage('unbind-DT', 'x1')
      get(input$select)[1:5,1:3]
    })
    data2 <- reactive({
      req(input$select)
      session$sendCustomMessage('unbind-DT', 'x2')
      get(input$select)[5:10,1:3]      
    })
    # render datatable with inputs
    output$x1 <- DT::renderDataTable({
      data.frame(data(),ENTER = shinyInput(numericInput,"numin",nrow(data()),value=NULL))
    },server=FALSE,escape=FALSE,selection='none',
    options=list(language = list(search = 'Filter:'),preDrawCallback=JS(
      'function() {
      Shiny.unbindAll(this.api().table().node());}'),
      drawCallback= JS(
        'function(settings) {
        Shiny.bindAll(this.api().table().node());}')))
    
    output$x2 <- DT::renderDataTable({
      data.frame(data2(),ENTER = shinyInput(numericInput,"numin2",nrow(data2()),value=NULL))
    },server=FALSE,escape=FALSE,selection='none',
    options=list(language = list(search = 'Filter:'),preDrawCallback=JS(
      'function() {
      Shiny.unbindAll(this.api().table().node());}'),
      drawCallback= JS(
        'function(settings) {
        Shiny.bindAll(this.api().table().node());}')))    
  }
)
